Rules / Modernization

SK1030 Use ??=

x = x ?? y is x ??= y.

CategoryModernization
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeSyntax
Needs a compilationno
Runs under --load=looseyes
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floorC# 8.0
Since0.6
SupersedesIDE0074

Why

The compound form says the intent once instead of naming the target twice, and it is the form that cannot drift — a rename that misses one of the two occurrences of x turns the long form into a silent bug.

Example

Instead of:

_cache = _cache ?? new Dictionary<string, int>();

Write:

_cache ??= new Dictionary<string, int>();

When it does not fire

Only fires when the assignment target and the left operand of the ?? are the same expression syntactically, and that expression is a chain of plain identifiers (x, this.x, a.b.c) — never an element access and never anything containing a call, because a[i] = a[i] ?? b evaluates the indexer twice and a[i] ??= b evaluates it once, which for a side-effecting indexer is a different program.
